# Cookie conformance vectors (T-COOKIE-CONFORMANCE-VECTORS-1).
#
# A pinned table of "what was set" -> "what is sent back", so the cookie
# module's adherence is a NUMBER rather than a claim. The prose lives in
# doc/conformance/rfc6265_cookies.md; this file is the ratchet that keeps it
# honest, per that register's own anti-rot rule.
#
# Seeded from RFC 6265bis's normative examples and the shape of the `http-state`
# vectors. Not a copy of either: those suites assume an HTTP client harness we
# do not have, and several of their cases turn on parsing quirks we deliberately
# reject. Every vector here is one this engine can be held to.
#
# FORMAT — blank line separates cases, each case gets a FRESH jar:
#   # comment
#   case <name>
#   set  <url> | <Set-Cookie value>
#   get  <url> | <expected Cookie header, or nothing for "send none">
#   xfail <T-TICKET-ID> <why>      (optional; must precede `get`)
#
# A vector that does not pass must be marked `xfail` and NAME THE TICKET that
# would fix it. An unexplained failure is not allowed to sit here going amber.

case basic set and get
set https://example.com/ | a=1
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case a cookie is not sent to a different host
set https://example.com/ | a=1
get https://other.com/ |

case host-only by default, so no subdomain
set https://example.com/ | a=1
get https://sub.example.com/ |

case an explicit Domain covers subdomains
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Domain=example.com
get https://sub.example.com/ | a=1

case a leading dot on Domain is ignored
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Domain=.example.com
get https://sub.example.com/ | a=1

case Domain may not widen to a different site
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Domain=other.com
get https://other.com/ |

case Domain may not be a public suffix
set https://example.co.uk/ | a=1; Domain=co.uk
get https://other.co.uk/ |

case a cookie set on a subdomain is not sent to the parent
set https://sub.example.com/ | a=1
get https://example.com/ |

case default path is the directory of the request
set https://example.com/dir/page.html | a=1
get https://example.com/dir/other.html | a=1

case default path does not leak to the parent directory
set https://example.com/dir/page.html | a=1
get https://example.com/ |

case an explicit path is honoured
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Path=/dir
get https://example.com/dir | a=1

case a path prefix must end at a boundary
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Path=/dir
get https://example.com/dirty |

case Secure cookies are withheld from http
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Secure
get http://example.com/ |

case Secure cookies are sent over https
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Secure
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case a later Set-Cookie replaces the same name
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | a=2
get https://example.com/ | a=2

case name and path together identify a cookie
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | a=2; Path=/dir
get https://example.com/dir | a=2; a=1

case Max-Age=0 deletes
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Max-Age=0
get https://example.com/ |

case a negative Max-Age deletes
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Max-Age=-1
get https://example.com/ |

case an expired Expires deletes
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Expires=Wed, 01 Jan 2020 00:00:00 GMT
get https://example.com/ |

case Max-Age wins over Expires
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Expires=Wed, 01 Jan 2020 00:00:00 GMT; Max-Age=3600
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case a cookie with no value is kept
set https://example.com/ | a=
get https://example.com/ | a=

case a valueless cookie with no equals sign is rejected
set https://example.com/ | novalue
get https://example.com/ |

case whitespace around the value is trimmed
set https://example.com/ | a=  1
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case a quoted value keeps its quotes
set https://example.com/ | a="1"
get https://example.com/ | a="1"

case several cookies are all returned
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | b=2
get https://example.com/ | a=1; b=2

case longer paths sort first
set https://example.com/ | a=1
set https://example.com/ | b=2; Path=/dir/sub
set https://example.com/ | c=3; Path=/dir
get https://example.com/dir/sub/page | b=2; c=3; a=1

case __Secure- requires Secure
set https://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1
get https://example.com/ |

case __Secure- is accepted with Secure
set https://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1; Secure
get https://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1

case __Secure- cannot be planted over http
set http://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1; Secure
get https://example.com/ |

# RFC 6265bis is asymmetric here and it is easy to read the wrong way round:
# SS4.1.3 tells servers to match case-SENSITIVELY when producing a prefixed
# cookie; SS5.4 tells user agents they MUST match case-INSENSITIVELY when
# consuming one. We are a user agent. The reason is a real bypass
# (httpwg/http-extensions#2231): server frameworks that compare cookie names
# case-insensitively would treat an attacker's insecure `__secure-session` as
# the protected `__Secure-session`.
case a differently cased secure prefix still faces the prefix conditions
set http://example.com/ | __secure-a=1
get http://example.com/ |

case a differently cased secure prefix is accepted when it meets them
set https://example.com/ | __sECuRe-a=1; Secure
get https://example.com/ | __sECuRe-a=1

# Matching the prefix case-insensitively does NOT merge the cookies: the names
# are still distinct, so both are stored and both are sent.
case prefixed cookies differing only in case remain distinct cookies
set https://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1; Secure
set https://example.com/ | __secure-a=2; Secure
get https://example.com/ | __Secure-a=1; __secure-a=2

case __Host- requires Secure, host-only and path slash
set https://example.com/ | __Host-a=1; Secure; Path=/
get https://example.com/ | __Host-a=1

case __Host- rejects an explicit Domain
set https://example.com/ | __Host-a=1; Secure; Domain=example.com; Path=/
get https://example.com/ |

case __Host- rejects a non-root path
set https://example.com/ | __Host-a=1; Secure; Path=/dir
get https://example.com/dir |

case __Host- cannot be planted over http
set http://example.com/ | __Host-a=1; Secure; Path=/
get https://example.com/ |

case a differently cased host prefix still faces the prefix conditions
set http://example.com/ | __host-a=1
get http://example.com/ |

case a differently cased host prefix is accepted when it meets them
set https://example.com/ | __hOsT-a=1; Secure; Path=/
get https://example.com/ | __hOsT-a=1

case an ordinary Secure cookie cannot be planted over http
set http://example.com/ | a=1; Secure
get https://example.com/ |

case an unknown attribute is ignored
set https://example.com/ | a=1; Fictional=yes
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case attribute names are case-insensitive
set https://example.com/ | a=1; SECURE
get http://example.com/ |

case a cookie name is case-sensitive
set https://example.com/ | A=1
set https://example.com/ | a=2
get https://example.com/ | A=1; a=2

case the port is not part of cookie scope
set https://example.com:8443/ | a=1
get https://example.com/ | a=1

case an empty Set-Cookie is ignored
set https://example.com/ |
get https://example.com/ |
